shots.title: WHY CLOCKS RUN SLOWER NEAR A BLACK HOLE
shots.purpose: Stage the thought experiment: a clock parked beside a dark horizon
shots.claim: a clock near a black hole ticks slower than a distant one
shots.evidence: full-bleed dark plate: glowing accretion disk around a black disc, small clock silhouette in orbit
shots.motion_reason: slow push-in: stillness first so the question lands clean
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the two-clock comparison

subject_contract.expected_subject: dark astronomical plate of a black hole with a bright accretion ring and a small clock silhouette nearby
required: bright ring or disk around it

one_second.relationship: a lone clock beside a dark horizon

shots.purpose: Frame the comparison: identical clocks, different rates
shots.claim: the slowdown is not mechanical: time itself runs slower
shots.evidence: two identical engraved clocks, one deep in the dark well, one far out in parchment sky
shots.motion_reason: hold the pair; the position difference is the information
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the spacetime funnel

subject_contract.expected_subject: two identical round clocks in one frame, one near a dark mass, one in open sky, vintage engraving style
required: dark mass edge near the lower clock

one_second.relationship: same clocks, different depths, different rates

shots.purpose: Reveal curved spacetime: the grid funnels down toward the hole
shots.claim: gravity stretches time; deeper in the field, the stretch is stronger
shots.evidence: diagram card: curved grid funnel with clock circles at depths, rust depth markers
shots.motion_reason: push down the funnel while depth markers carry the information
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the horizon detail

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment diagram of a curved spacetime grid funneling toward a dark disc with small clock circles at depths
required: curved grid lines forming a funnel

one_second.relationship: deeper in the funnel, slower the clock

shots.purpose: Rest the eye at the edge: light bending around the horizon
shots.claim: light itself bends near the horizon
shots.evidence: tight macro of engraved light curves skimming a dark edge
shots.motion_reason: slow zoom reveals the bending curves
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the dilation curve card

subject_contract.expected_subject: engraved close-up of light rays curving around a dark circular edge

one_second.relationship: even light follows the curve of the well

shots.purpose: Explain the mechanism with a measured curve: clock rate versus depth
shots.claim: in general relativity, clocks deeper in a gravitational field tick fewer seconds
shots.evidence: graph card: clock rate dropping with depth along a drawn curve, axis ticks marked
shots.motion_reason: drift along the curve so its drop reads as the effect
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the satellite network

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment graph card showing a falling curve of clock rate against distance from a mass

one_second.relationship: the deeper the clock, the lower its rate

shots.purpose: Ground the effect: a probe's clock runs measurably slow near the disk
shots.claim: a probe near the mass carries a clock that falls behind
shots.evidence: probe silhouette with a large clock face skimming above the glowing disk
shots.motion_reason: slow drift with the probe; the clock face is the annotation
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the GPS card

subject_contract.expected_subject: vintage-engraving probe silhouette with a round clock face, skimming above a glowing accretion disk

one_second.relationship: the probe's clock reads behind the distant one

shots.purpose: Escalate into the measurable world: the GPS constellation's corrected clocks
shots.claim: GPS satellite clocks gain about 38 microseconds per day without relativistic corrections
shots.evidence: diagram card: Earth disc with orbit ring, satellite dots, 38-microsecond figure popped
shots.motion_reason: orbit ring drifts the eye around the corrected clocks
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the horizon freeze

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment diagram of Earth with an orbital ring of small satellites and a rust time correction figure

shots.purpose: Twist: the same fall looks different from outside and inside
shots.claim: at the event horizon the dilation grows without limit for a distant observer
shots.evidence: split card: probe falling locally on one side, frozen at the rim from afar on the other
shots.motion_reason: the split transforms as the two views resolve side by side
shots.transition_reason: hard cut to the payoff clock

subject_contract.expected_subject: parchment split card: left panel probe crossing a dark edge normally, right panel the same probe frozen as a faint image on the rim

one_second.relationship: falling in locally, frozen from far away

shots.purpose: Land the payoff: the clock against the sky, its rate owned by gravity
shots.claim: time keeps ticking everywhere, but gravity sets its rate
shots.evidence: dusk-sky clock silhouette plate reprising the opening darkness
shots.motion_reason: slow pull to rest; the strongest composition holds still

subject_contract.expected_subject: single engraved clock face silhouetted against a dark dusk sky with a faint accretion ring on the horizon
required: faint glow ring near the horizon

one_second.relationship: the clock still ticking, just slower
